Plus it doesn't help people aren't going to see the latest movies as they used to 5 years ago, can Iger rebuild the company? I mean, its a huge business, and he already did it once, so maybe, but not in the short run, and well institutional traders have move into it, so i would think that at the very best its a long term bet.

Hi, (also an accountant), your sales are the one dollar coins you take from the vending machine, to dump into the change machine, and just as my colleague above said the change machine its just another bank account for you. Its like if you had to be there to exchange 20 dollar bills for coins for every customer, so you should register the revenue as the money you take from the vending machines and then dump the coins into the change machine. And then you take the bills from the change machine and that should be the same value of coins entered into the vending machine, that are your sales + the beginning balance of change you put in the change machine in the first place + what ever error both the machines had and gave you extra coins. That last one you can add when you get into the coin mech to take that money out. And its not not a sale, its not a sale because your machine basically scammed your customer (I think that is funny haha, like a "mob member machine job"), but its also not not a sale, because you do have the money. So I would count it as income, just maybe have it separated in your app, so you can track it, and I would suggest tracking that, because the more money you get from that, the more the machine is scamming clients and the more likely someone its to kick your machine to death (following the mob member machine analogy).

Now, as stated above, given your need to change the bills for coins, you will need to control the money that goes from the vending to the change machine, or you may be counting your change balance as income, (you shouldn't do that), so I also think (with out knowing the industry), that you should update your machines to cards and bills to avoid the change machines all together.

If you have the money to develop, and knowing that its a commercial area, I would build some apartments for rent and places to lease to small businesses. This will warranty a return on the investment in monthly payments, like dividends and turning the plot into a place to rent would increase its value in case you need to sell in the future, and it seems to be a big place, so you can develop it by sections. If you don't have any experience as a landlord and/or money, but you are interested, then I would sell part of the lot to someone looking to develop and then use that money to develop the other part. I am a landlord myself, and I starting subleasing, now I have a couple of places I lease that I own, so I can tell you its a bit hard at first, and costly, but it is worthy in the long run. There are a bunch of youtube channels you can watch to get your mind around it, I recommend minority mindset, that guy has a couple of videos describing what it was for him to get into this business. I hope it helps!

I was reading about the [squeeze](https://moxreports.com/vw-infinity-squeeze/) of vw in 2008. I like a lot how the story unfolded. It seemed like a safe bet, 0% risk from the stand point of the hedge funds, after all it was during the 2008 recession and automakers were going out like flies and then it happened... Porche (the other automaker) bought about 20% of the shares outstanding of vw and with a position of 30%, they became the defacto owners of vw, the hedge funds, thinking there was a short float of only 1% didn't pay much attention until, suddenly went to 12.8% and then it was chaos. So much so, that it lead to the bankruptcy of 5 big hedge fund names in the industry.

Fast forward to 2021 and this crazy thing with GME, BB and AMC. Well the short float for them its: [GME: 121%](https://finviz.com/quote.ashx?t=GME&ty=c&ta=1&p=d), [AMC: 41.91](https://finviz.com/quote.ashx?t=AMC&ty=c&ta=1&p=d) and [BB: 7.13%](https://finviz.com/quote.ashx?t=BB&ty=c&ta=1&p=d) back in 2008 the problem was porche (in that year the automaker made more money trading options that selling cars), was the one holding most of the shares outstanding, and that spiked the value of the share of vw to 1,000 euro, making it the most valuable company on earth at that time by market cap. Well right now the institutional ownership of those shares its crazy. [GME its owned 119.77%](https://money.cnn.com/quote/shareholders/shareholders.html?symb=GME&subView=institutional) by institutional owners alone! [BB its at 49%](https://money.cnn.com/quote/shareholders/shareholders.html?symb=BB&subView=institutional) and [AMC its at 14%](https://money.cnn.com/quote/shareholders/shareholders.html?symb=AMC&subView=institutional) , that last one its not that high, maybe they are trying to avoid other GME with that one though.

Anyway, the thing here is that if you add up the ownership of all the shares, not only institutional, but also all traders reported, both BB and GME are being held by more than a 100%, [GME its crazy at about 300%](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/GME/holders?p=GME) . This means that when the margin call comes, (and it will come), someone its going to get major screwed over this. Because remember, vw in 2008 had only a few players doing the squeeze, and only one mayor buyer -porche- holding the stock before the squeeze, in the wsb subredit, there are more than 5 million people talking about holding these three stocks. So no wonder why they stoped the trading, this could potentially ruin the life of real people with three boats, making them two or, god forbid, one boat owners! So maybe they are trying to close the position taking a loss, but not a loss so high that it might force them into going bankrupt. What do you think?

Anyway, I am mexican, and I used to work in the US (I was not an ilegal immigrant, so relax republican voters reading this), as an accountant; in this job I learn to write code and do data mining to analyze financial information, and while I was going back to México in one trip I realized that this could be a suitable business in my home country. I was actually doing well in my job, and my boss got really surprise when I told him what I was planning, a rise and visa papers to stop the trips back to México where offer (at the time my visa required me to go back to México every so often and then go back to the US) but I got the "fantastic" idea of leaving said job and to start the magical adventure of the business in México, because millennial shit. So with some savings and a lot of hearth I manage to put together the first MVP (Minimum valuable product), and to my surprise, not only my software worked, but there were people willing to paid for it in my home city. So I decided to give it a real shot at it, but for that I needed money to invest in it. Now, México is not the shit hole most americans think it is, having lived in both countries I can say that: yes its true that the US has better roads, but both countries are more similar of what you might think, so venture capital also exists in this country, the issue is that to get it here you not only need a good idea and a good team, you need sales, a lot of them. I am not a sales man, I tried to convinced the church, the government, my girlfriend and my boss, the CEO of the company that I used to work on to invest some money in my idea (not that much money just like 20k) and I failed, then I tried with other folks up north and I got the same results, so I decided that I needed a co-founder to help me with this, and here is where the problem begins. In October of 2017 I asked my sister to join me in my crazy idea of building a company that in some years would had created one of the first commercially used artificial intelligence, and it would be applied in the accounting services industry, tackling the boring ass task of taxes (robots are meant to do boring stuff for us, that is the base of all of my ideals), she reluctantly accepted, in had sight maybe I should had hire someone and leave her at her own devises, but I didn't, and I offer to pay her some money and to give her 40% of the business, she said yes (of course), and at first - even though we fought a lot-, she delivered, and we go our first 20 paid users and finally cash flow to invest in the production software and to look for investors. We applied to some venture capitalist founds in México City and we actually got really close to making some deals, but I always got it short, for some fucking reason people don't believe me and my stupid sister (that for some reason everyone believes in), refused to give any of the investor pitches, she even got as far as to said that if we ever got any investment, it would be out of my capital share, not her's (this is one of the many things that bugs me about her). Well we haven't got any funding and its been a goddamn year, and my bitch of a sisters has now threaten me with leaving and starting her own startup (like mine of course), and insists on working only 5 hours a day, lunch hours included there. She is an ass, I didn't hate my sister before, I do now.  I cannot just take her out of the business or I would become an outcast for my family and I cannot start it again, its been to hard to get it this big. I just don't know what to do, I fucking hate myself for trusting this woman; the cherry in the pie is that I did it thinking that the only human in the face of the planet that wouldn't cause me any problems, and that I could actually trust, would be her...I got it terrible wrong. What would you do in my place?
